children: Bitcoin
trades at $61,568, now below the $62,862 an average major miner pays to produce one coin. Network computing power remains near its peak, yet on-chain data now leans negative.
The price is down 2.6% over the past 24 hours. It sits about 50% below its October 2025 all-time high of $126,080.
Bitcoin Mining Cost Floor Faces Its Third Test of 2026
CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju flagged the move on November 18. He warned that a break lower could pressure public miners and their institutional backers.
The estimate comes from CryptoQuant data based on MARA Holdings filings. It puts the average cost of mining one BTC at $62,862 for the third quarter of 2026.

This marks the third time BTC has tested the line this year. In February, the price dropped to the cost level near $64,000. In June and July, it briefly slipped below the roughly $60,000 quarterly cost before recovering.

However, the figure reflects one company rather than the whole industry. MARA ranks among the largest miners, so smaller operators likely face higher costs and thinner margins. For comparison, JPMorgan’s production cost
stood at $85,000 in late September.
Hashrate Nears Its Record as Miners Keep Investing
Ki Young Ju also noted that hashrate remains high despite the squeeze. In his view, public miners are still betting on a long-term bull market.
Glassnode data supports that reading. The 30-day average hashrate stands near 1.02 zettahashes per second (ZH/s). That is less than 10% below the record of about 1.1 ZH/s set in November 2025.

More notably, hashrate and price have moved in opposite directions. Since early October, hashrate has climbed more than 10% from about 915 exahashes per second (EH/s). Over the same period, BTC has lost more than 25%.
Meanwhile, the network shows no sign of miner capitulation. In past downturns, falling hashrate signaled operators switching off unprofitable machines. That has not happened, even as some miners
power to Artificial Intelligence
Still, hashrate tends to lag price. Mining hardware is ordered months in advance. Part of the recent growth may reflect machines bought when BTC traded near $87,000.
On-Chain Indicators Flip Bearish, Analyst Warns

In contrast, on-chain data paints a weaker near-term picture. Julio Moreno is Head of Research at CryptoQuant and a member of BeInCrypto’s Market Intelligence Experts Council. He says the market has turned.
There’s no sugarcoating it, by basically all metrics, Bitcoin returned to a bearish phase.
According to Moreno, both spot and speculative demand have contracted sharply since late October. He added that the analysts CryptoQuant tracks are the most bearish since November 2025.
Price has also broken almost every key on-chain and technical support, he noted. The warning adds to other bearish signals that appeared after BTC’s rebound earlier this week.
His chart of long-term holder

spending by price level shows where the remaining support sits. The densest 2026 cluster lies between $62,500 and $65,000. On many days at those prices, 30-day LTH spending reached 250,000 to 475,000 BTC.
Below $62,000, that activity thins out sharply. Moreno acknowledged some capitulation, with holders realizing large daily losses. However, he warned there is still room for more selling.
Bitcoin Mining Cost and $62,000 Floor
Three separate signals now converge near the same price. The mining cost stands at $62,862, the recent low at aorund $61,00, and the densest LTH cluster begins at $62,500.

A sustained break below $62,000 would remove both the miner floor and the strongest remaining on-chain support. In that case, $60,000 becomes the next level to watch, followed by the 2026 low near $57,700.
On the upside, BTC would need to reclaim $65,000 to clear the LTH cluster. The next heavy zone, between $76,000 and $82,000, could then act as resistance.

Macro conditions add pressure. US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have recorded about $2.6 billion in net outflows in November. Minutes from the Federal Reserve’s latest meeting have also revived talk of a December rate hike.
Both camps may prove right. Moreno still sees BTC in a value zone, yet he cautions that a recovery could take time.
Yes, Bitcoin price is in a value zone, but, historically, a bottoming process and subsequent recovery has taken months, even if there are short-term rallies in the process.
Miners, for now, appear willing to wait out that process. Whether the $62,000 floor holds may decide how long they have to.

title: Bitcoin Falls to Mining Cost Level as Hashrate Nears Record and Indicators Flip Bearish
